hazmatProfile.spillCategory: Large Spill (9,000 lb high-pressure receiver manifold fracture)
hazmatProfile.tacticalRule: ERG 2024 Guide 125 (UN1005 Large Spill): Isolate 500 ft in all directions; protect 0.5 mi (day) / 1.3 mi (night) downwind. Use water fog/spray downwind on vapor cloud only — NEVER apply direct water stream into liquid ammonia pool.

erg2024.notes: Corrosive & toxic inhalation hazard (TIH); water fog/spray on vapor cloud, do NOT apply water directly into liquid spill.
Heavy greenish-yellow TIH gas; settles in low river valleys; shelter-in-place with HVAC shutoff when evacuation would cross plume.
Polar solvent — requires Alcohol-Resistant Aqueous Film-Forming Foam (AR-AFFF); tank car in fire: isolate 0.5 mile (800 m) in all directions.
BLEVE hazard if tank car/vessel exposed to flame; isolate 1 mile (1600 m) in all directions if tank is involved in fire.

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.topic: Governor's State of Emergency & Preparedness Proclamation
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Authorizes Governor (or Legislature by concurrent resolution) to proclaim a state of emergency; activates emergency powers and state EOP.

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.topic: Local Emergency Organization & Mutual Aid Arrangements
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Authorizes county/municipal emergency services directors and reciprocal intrastate mutual aid across West Virginia political subdivisions.
Governs interstate mutual aid requests, credential reciprocity, tort liability, and reimbursement through WVEMD.

wvStatutesAndDoctrine.cite: WV HB 5638 / WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol
wvStatutesAndDoctrine.rule: Requires immediate isolation of compromised OT/IT segments, preservation of forensic logs, and coordination with WVOT CISO / WV Fusion Center—prohibits unapproved ransom payments.
EMPG recipients must maintain a progressive HSEEP exercise program and submit a completed After-Action Report / Improvement Plan (AAR/IP) within 90 calendar days.

T&M contracts are restricted to a reasonable initial emergency window (typically <= 70 hours under FEMA PA guidance), require a strict dollar ceiling, and require independent load/scale/monitor verification.

briefing.executiveSummary: At 05:42 EST, a severe Appalachian ice storm snaps a 34.5 kV feeder serving the {SEAT} riverfront industrial corridor in {COUNTY} County ({WVEMD_AREA}). When backup diesel power transfers at Valley Cold Storage, hydraulic shock fractures a corroded relief manifold on a 9,000 lb Anhydrous Ammonia (UN1005) receiver, releasing a dense white toxic inhalation hazard (TIH) cloud hugging the {RIVER_BASIN} terrace under a 24°F temperature inversion. Sixteen minutes later (05:58 EST), operators at the {SEAT} Municipal Water Treatment Plant discover their SCADA HMI locked by ransomware after unauthorized commands throttled High-Service Pumps 2 and 3—dropping distribution main pressure toward 18 psi just as Fire/Hazmat crews, the Regional Medical Center, and an 84-bed nursing home 0.38 miles downwind require coordinated protective action.

keyTimelines.event: 0.65 in. radial ice downs primary feeder in {SEAT}; Valley Cold Storage receiver manifold fractures (UN1005, 9,000 lb).
911 receives pungent ammonia odor reports along Riverview Terrace; icy secondary grades slow mutual-aid response.
Municipal Water SCADA HMI displays ransom note; High-Service Pumps 2 & 3 throttled; main pressure drops from 62 psi toward 19 psi.
{COUNTY} County EOC activates ({WVEMD_AREA}); Exercise Clock starts at T+00m across 6 agency seats.

objectives.text: Execute ERG 2024 Guide 125 protective actions for a 9,000 lb UN1005 release (500 ft isolation, 0.5 mi daytime shelter-in-place with HVAC shutoff, vapor-only fog knockdown) within 10 minutes of arrival.
Isolate compromised water SCADA OT/IT segments, restore manual pump pressure above 20 psi, preserve forensic artifacts, and report to WVOT CISO / WV Fusion Center per WV HB 5638.
Counter viral evacuation misinformation on iced valley bridges with a verified <= 120-word IPAWS/WEA warning meeting all 7 HSEEP Public Warning Essentials.

Align county mutual aid (W. Va. Code § 15-5-8 & § 15-5-11), Governor State of Emergency escalation (§ 15-5-6), FEMA-compliant <= 70-hour T&M debris caps (2 CFR §§ 200.318–200.327), and 90-day EMPG AAR/IP tracking.

groundRules: HSEEP No-Fault Environment: Evaluate systems, plans, and cross-agency handoffs—not individual personnel.
Fog-of-War Discipline: Switch your Role Pill above to view seat-specific intelligence; share critical dependencies verbally across agencies.
Statutory & Technical Grounding: Anchor tactical calls in ERG 2024 Guide 125, W. Va. Code Chapter 15 Article 5, WV HB 5638, and 2 CFR Part 200.

roles.title: Master Facilitator & White Cell Evaluator
roles.summary: Full visibility across hazmat dispersion, water SCADA pressure dependencies, hospital walk-in surge, and statutory compliance gates.
knownFacts: HIDDEN INTERDEPENDENCY #1: Fire Engine 11 hydrant supply in the industrial corridor is fed by the exact municipal water zone losing pressure from the SCADA cyber intrusion.

HIDDEN INTERDEPENDENCY #2: Valley Nursing Home (84 oxygen-dependent residents) sits at 0.38 mi ENE—inside the 0.5 mi UN1005 plume—where 0.65 in. road ice makes evacuation into open air far deadlier than Shelter-in-Place + HVAC shutoff.
HIDDEN INTERDEPENDENCY #3: 14 self-evacuated motorists are walking straight into the {SEAT} Regional Medical Center ED wearing ammonia-saturated winter coats.

PROCUREMENT & STATUTORY TRAP: At T+48m, an ice-debris contractor will push an uncapped 30-day Time-and-Materials contract; FEMA PA caps emergency T&M at <= 70 hours with a hard dollar ceiling and independent load monitoring.
blindSpots: Facilitator note: Watch whether Water SCADA notifies Fire IC and Hospital BEFORE hydrant and decon pressure drops below 20 psi.
priorityQuestions: Which seat first identifies the shared dependency between SCADA pump throttling, Hazmat decon water, and Hospital chillers?
Does the PIO explicitly refute the false Valley Bridge evacuation rumor inside 120 words?
Does County Commission / EOC enforce the <= 70-hour T&M ceiling and route state requests through WVEMD?

roles.title: WVOT Cyber Incident Response & Municipal Water SCADA Lead
roles.summary: Contains ransomware intrusion on water treatment OT/IT systems, restores manual pumping pressure, and preserves forensic evidence.
knownFacts: At 05:58 EST, the SCADA engineering workstation displayed a ransom note demanding 0.8 BTC; remote RDP session originated via a vendor VPN jump host.
Unauthorized Modbus commands throttled High-Service Pumps 2 & 3 to 15%, dropping clearwell discharge pressure to 19 psi (regulatory Boil Water threshold is < 20 psi).
Plant electricians confirm High-Service Pumps 2 & 3 have physical HAND-OFF-AUTO switches allowing local manual VFD operation once disconnected from the SCADA PLC network.
WV HB 5638 & WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol mandate immediate network isolation, forensic log preservation, CISO/WV Fusion Center notification, and zero unapproved ransom payment.
blindSpots: You do NOT initially know that Fire/Hazmat is actively drawing water for UN1005 vapor fogging and winter mass decon unless coordinated through EOC.
priorityQuestions: How fast can we air-gap the OT PLC cabinet and switch pumps to manual local control without wiping volatile forensic memory?
Which zones dropped below 20 psi requiring an immediate precautionary Boil Water Advisory via DoHS / PIO?
Have WVOT CISO and the WV Fusion Center been formally notified under WV HB 5638?

roles.title: {SEAT} Regional Medical Center EM & WV DoHS Public Health

knownFacts: 14 walk-in patients just arrived at the ED ambulance vestibule in private cars wearing heavy winter coats smelling strongly of ammonia (zero field decon performed).
Warm indoor hospital air rapidly volatilizes ammonia trapped in winter wool/synthetics—if admitted straight into the ED, secondary off-gassing can incapacitate staff and force ED closure.
Valley Nursing Home (0.38 mi ENE of leak) houses 84 residents (19 on continuous oxygen); transferring frail seniors onto iced roads through the plume carries high mortality risk.
Hospital domestic water pressure gauge just triggered a low-pressure alarm; internal emergency water tank holds ~6 hours at surge consumption.
blindSpots: You do NOT know how long municipal water pressure will remain impaired or whether more walk-in casualties are inbound from Valley Bridge.
priorityQuestions: How do we lock down ED doors/HVAC and stand up heated exterior winter decon (24°F) so patients avoid both secondary off-gassing and hypothermia?
How do we verify Valley Nursing Home maintenance has shut off fresh-air HVAC intakes and sealed dampers?
Do we need the Potable Water Tanker Task Force dispatched to the hospital manifold now?

injects.title: Engine 11 On-Scene Size-Up & ERG 2024 UN1005 Protective Action
injects.prompt: Engine 11 arrives upwind of Valley Cold Storage in {SEAT}. Facility engineers confirm a fractured manifold on a 9,000 lb Anhydrous Ammonia (UN1005) receiver venting a low, dense white cloud ENE (065°) along {RIVER_BASIN} toward the iced Valley Bridge (0.29 mi) and Valley Nursing Home (0.38 mi, 84 residents). Crew wears structural bunker gear + SCBA; Regional Hazmat Level A entry is 22 minutes out. What immediate tactical order does Unified Command issue?

options.label: Option A
options.summary: Isolate 500 ft in all directions; order 0.5 mi ENE Shelter-in-Place + HVAC shutoff; apply downwind water fog on vapor cloud ONLY (never on liquid pool); hold Level A entry.
options.rationale: Matches ERG 2024 Guide 125 for a Large Spill of UN1005 (500 ft initial isolation; 0.5 mi daytime downwind protection). Shelter-in-place with HVAC shutoff protects 84 nursing home residents without exposing them on iced roads, and fogging vapor (not pooled liquid ammonia) prevents violent exothermic boil-off and structural-gear skin burns.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 (UN1005 Large Spill: 500 ft Isolation / 0.5 mi Day Downwind; Water Fog on Vapor Only)

options.label: Option B
options.summary: Set a 100 ft small-spill perimeter and begin loading ambulatory nursing home residents onto transit buses while Engine 11 stands by.
options.rationale: Misapplies the ERG 2024 Small Spill row (100 ft / 0.1 mi) to a 9,000 lb Large Spill (500 ft / 0.5 mi) and exposes frail seniors to outdoor plume concentrations during slow icy boarding.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 (Small vs. Large Spill Table Mismatch — 9,000 lb requires 500 ft / 0.5 mi)
options.cascadeAlert: UNDER-SIZED 100 FT PERIMETER & OUTDOOR BUS EXPOSURE (Inject 1 — Option B): Low inversion held UN1005 vapor across the 150–450 ft zone and nursing home loading ramp, generating 11 additional acute inhalation patients and straining EMS!

options.label: Option C
options.summary: Advance Engine 11 in structural bunker gear + SCBA to flow a straight 500 gpm master stream directly into the liquid ammonia manifold pit to dilute the leak.
options.rationale: Direct water into pooled liquid anhydrous ammonia triggers an exothermic reaction that violently accelerates toxic vapor generation, rapidly drains failing water mains, and exposes firefighters in non-vapor-tight structural gear to severe chemical skin burns.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 CRITICAL WARNING ("Do NOT direct water at spill or source of leak"; Level A required)
options.cascadeAlert: VIOLENT AMMONIA VAPOR SURGE & FIREFIGHTER BURNS (Inject 1 — Option C): Direct water stream into liquid UN1005 boiled off a concentrated plume surge across the nursing home, injured two Engine 11 personnel, and accelerated municipal water pressure collapse!

options.label: Option D
options.summary: Order an immediate general evacuation of all valley residents and facilities eastward across the Valley Bridge.
options.rationale: Directs civilian vehicles onto 0.65 in. of ice straight through the 0.5 mi ENE toxic inhalation plume with car defrosters pulling outside air into cabins.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 Protective Action Decision Factors (In-Place Protection vs. Evacuation Through Plume)
options.cascadeAlert: ICY VALLEY BRIDGE GRIDLOCK INSIDE PLUME (Inject 1 — Option D): Over 60 civilian cars slid to a standstill on the iced Valley Bridge directly inside the 0.5 mi UN1005 plume, creating a multi-vehicle mass-casualty rescue crisis!

injects.targetSeat: WVOT Cyber & Water SCADA + County EOC
injects.title: Municipal Water SCADA Ransomware & Distribution Pressure Drop (<20 psi)
injects.prompt: The {SEAT} Municipal Water Plant Chief Operator reports the SCADA HMI screen is locked with a 0.8 BTC ransom demand. Unauthorized commands throttled High-Service Pumps 2 & 3, dropping distribution pressure from 62 psi to 19 psi—threatening Engine 11 fog lines, heated decon showers, Regional Medical Center chillers, and crossing the <20 psi regulatory backflow threshold. How do WVOT Cyber and Water Operations respond?

options.label: Option A
options.summary: Sever IT/OT network bridge immediately (preserving forensic memory/logs), switch High-Service Pumps to local manual VFD hand-control (>45 psi), report to WVOT CISO & WV Fusion Center, refuse ransom, and issue precautionary Boil Water Advisory for <20 psi zones.
options.rationale: Satisfies WV HB 5638 and WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol (containment, forensic preservation, mandatory reporting, zero unapproved ransom payment) while restoring hydraulic pressure for Fire/Hazmat and Hospital operations within minutes and protecting public health under the <20 psi Boil Water rule.
options.citation: WV HB 5638 / WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol & WV Bureau for Public Health (<20 psi Boil Water Rule)

options.label: Option B
options.summary: Shut down all water treatment plant electrical breakers completely and wait 2 hours for an outside cyber contractor before restarting any pumps.
options.rationale: Contains lateral cyber movement, but shutting off all pumping drops municipal mains to 0 psi during an active hazmat decon and hospital surge emergency.
options.citation: WV HB 5638 & FEMA Core Capability: Infrastructure Systems (Containment without Manual Continuity)
options.cascadeAlert: ZERO-PSI HYDRANT & HOSPITAL WATER LOSS (Inject 2 — Option B): Full plant power-down collapsed municipal mains to 0 psi—cutting water to Hazmat decon showers and forcing {SEAT} Regional Medical Center onto its 6-hour reserve tank!

options.label: Option C
options.summary: Keep the SCADA network online so the utility business office can wire 0.8 BTC emergency ransom and obtain the decryption key quickly.
options.rationale: Violates WV HB 5638 / WVOT incident rules prohibiting unapproved ransom payments, leaves the threat actor in active control of water treatment actuators, and offers no guarantee of restoration.
options.citation: WV HB 5638 / WVOT Cyber Incident Protocol (Prohibits Unapproved Ransom Payment; Requires Immediate Isolation)
options.cascadeAlert: ACTIVE SCADA LATERAL INCURSION (Inject 2 — Option C): Leaving compromised OT networks live allowed the adversary to close Clearwell Discharge Valve 4 and exfiltrate credentials while ransom talks stalled, triggering a countywide Boil Water Order!

options.label: Option D
options.summary: Format and factory-wipe all SCADA servers and PLC logs immediately, then bridge the consoles onto municipal Wi-Fi to reboot.
options.rationale: Destroys volatile forensic evidence required by WVOT CIRT / WV Fusion Center under WV HB 5638 and re-exposes unsegmented OT controls to immediate re-compromise.
options.citation: WV HB 5638 Forensic Preservation & OT Network Segmentation Mandate
options.cascadeAlert: FORENSIC LOGS DESTROYED & OT RE-LOCKED (Inject 2 — Option D): Wiping HMI drives erased attacker IOCs needed by WVOT CIRT, and bridging over unsegmented Wi-Fi re-encrypted the console 9 minutes later!

injects.targetSeat: Hospital & DoHS Health + Fire & Hazmat IC
injects.title: Hospital ED Walk-In Contamination Surge & 24°F HVAC/Decon Decision
injects.prompt: Fourteen self-referred motorists and plant workers arrive unannounced at {SEAT} Regional Medical Center’s ED vestibule coughing with watering eyes, wearing heavy winter coats saturated with pungent ammonia vapor. Outside temperature is 24°F and municipal water pressure remains unstable. What protocol do Hospital Command and DoHS Health execute?

options.label: Option A
options.summary: Lock down main ED entrances & isolate ED zone HVAC return air; route walk-ins through a heated exterior decon tent (remove outer winter garments + tepid eye/skin flush); hook Potable Water Tanker to hospital manifold; coordinate DoHS surge triage.
options.rationale: Prevents secondary ammonia off-gassing from shutting down the county’s trauma/emergency department, removes 80–90% of contaminant immediately via outer garment removal in a heated shelter (preventing 24°F hypothermia), and sustains hospital water continuity.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 Decontamination · FEMA Core Capability: Public Health, Healthcare, and EMS

options.label: Option B
options.summary: Lock ED doors and wash walk-in patients outdoors on the open 24°F concrete apron using an unheated fire engine booster hose.
options.rationale: Protects the interior ED from secondary contamination, but cold-water drenching in 24°F freezing wind induces rapid hypothermia.
options.citation: Cold-Weather Mass Decontamination Doctrine & ERG 2024 Guide 125
options.cascadeAlert: ACUTE HYPOTHERMIA ADMISSIONS (Inject 3 — Option B): Unheated 24°F outdoor hosedown caused 5 cold-exposure admissions and slowed walk-in compliance at the hospital perimeter!

options.label: Option C
options.summary: Bring all 14 patients in their winter coats directly into the warm central ED waiting room and trauma bays to triage out of the freezing weather.
options.rationale: Ammonia trapped in heavy winter clothing rapidly volatilizes in warm indoor hospital air, incapacitating unprotected ED clinicians and forcing full Emergency Department closure.
options.citation: ERG 2024 Guide 125 Secondary Contamination Warning & Hospital HAZMAT Lockdown Standard
options.cascadeAlert: EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT FORCED ON FULL DIVERSION (Inject 3 — Option C): Secondary NH3 off-gassing inside the warm ED sickened 6 nurses and forced {SEAT} Regional Medical Center onto full ambulance diversion!

options.label: Option D
options.summary: Lock hospital gates and instruct symptomatic walk-ins to get back in their cars and drive 1.2 miles across iced streets to Fire Station 1.
options.rationale: Turning away unstable respiratory patients presenting on hospital property violates federal EMTALA screening/stabilization duties and puts impaired drivers onto iced streets.
options.citation: EMTALA (42 U.S.C. § 1395dd) & WV DoHS Hospital Surge Standard
options.cascadeAlert: EMTALA COMPLIANCE BREACH & MULTI-CAR SLIDEOFF (Inject 3 — Option D): Turning away symptomatic walk-ins triggered regulatory escalation and caused a secondary crash two blocks from the hospital!

injects.targetSeat: County EOC & WVEMD + PIO & County Commission
injects.title: Intrastate Mutual Aid, Debris T&M Ceiling & State of Emergency Proclamation
injects.prompt: Radial ice hits 0.75 in., blocking ridge feeders across {COUNTY} County. Overtime and mutual-aid costs mount. A private contractor offers the County Commission immediate tree/ice debris crews if Commissioners sign an uncapped 30-day Time-and-Materials (T&M) contract right now. How do County EOC and Commissioners structure statutory escalation and emergency contracting?

options.label: Option A
options.summary: Activate WV intrastate mutual aid (§ 15-5-8 & § 15-5-11), submit local declaration to WVEMD requesting a Governor State of Emergency Proclamation (§ 15-5-6; pre-staging EMAC § 15-5-22), and cap emergency T&M debris work strictly at <= 70 hours with a hard dollar ceiling and independent load monitors.
options.rationale: Aligns West Virginia emergency powers and mutual aid reimbursement channels while strictly preserving FEMA Public Assistance eligibility under 2 CFR §§ 200.318–200.327 and FEMA PAPPG.

options.label: Option B
options.summary: Enforce the <= 70-hour T&M contract cap locally, but hold off notifying WVEMD or requesting a W. Va. Code § 15-5-6 State Proclamation until next week’s damage tally.
options.rationale: Protects federal procurement compliance, but delaying WVEMD escalation bottlenecks state potable water tankers, WVOT on-site support, and {WVDOH_DIST} heavy equipment prioritization.
options.citation: W. Va. Code § 15-5-6 & § 15-5-8 (Delayed State EOC Escalation)
options.cascadeAlert: STATE RESOURCE BOTTLENECK (Inject 4 — Option B): Delaying W. Va. Code § 15-5-6 escalation through WVEMD pushed state tanker and heavy grader tasking back by 6+ hours.

options.label: Option C
options.summary: Sign the uncapped 30-day Time-and-Materials debris contract immediately using contractor self-certified load tickets so saws start rolling now.
options.rationale: Uncapped T&M contracts exceeding the ~70-hour initial emergency window without a not-to-exceed ceiling and independent monitoring are one of the top causes of FEMA Public Assistance audit clawbacks.
options.citation: 2 CFR §§ 200.318–200.327 & FEMA PAPPG (Uncapped T&M Cost Disallowance)
options.cascadeAlert: SEVERE FEMA PA AUDIT EXPOSURE (Inject 4 — Option C): Uncapped 30-day T&M debris contracting without independent load verification jeopardizes federal reimbursement under 2 CFR § 200.318(j)!

options.label: Option D
options.summary: Bypass WVEMD and phone an out-of-state private/municipal hazmat team directly across the state border to self-deploy immediately.
options.rationale: Interstate mutual aid deployed outside WVEMD Emergency Management Assistance Compact (EMAC) procedures lacks statutory tort immunity, credential reciprocity, and reimbursement authority.
options.citation: W. Va. Code § 15-5-22 (Emergency Management Assistance Compact — EMAC)
options.cascadeAlert: INTERSTATE LIABILITY & REIMBURSEMENT GAP (Inject 4 — Option D): Self-deploying out-of-state units outside WVEMD EMAC channels (W. Va. Code § 15-5-22) voided statutory liability protection and cost recovery!
